ai.description: Roux's Forest Calotes reaches 25 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct white or yellow stripe along the flanks and a dark patch before the shoulder. A low nuchal crest is present in both sexes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Monilesaurus rouxii* is best distinguished by the distinct, white or pale-colored spot located just above the tympanum, which is absent in other similar Indian agamas.
ai.habitat: *Monilesaurus rouxii* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, as well as coffee plantations, across the Western Ghats at elevations between 300 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Roux's Forest Calotes is primarily diurnal and often displays a defensive strategy of freezing motionless against tree trunks to blend into the bark using its camouflage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Monilesaurus rouxii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 4–8 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Monilesaurus rouxii* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring across Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at elevations up to 2,000 meters.
